raw_findings.message: The summary is created with mode 0666, so a permissive umask (including umask 0) makes potentially sensitive report contents readable and writable by everyone.
The gzip command's error is discarded, so the program returns success even when compression fails and the promised compressed output was not produced.
The output path is concatenated into a shell command without quoting, so a path containing shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary commands.
Setting workers to zero or less starts no consumers, leaving the job producer and the caller blocked indefinitely.
Deferring each file close until the worker exits keeps every file opened by that worker open while it processes later jobs, so many input files can exhaust the process's file descriptors.
Multiple workers increment the shared counts map without synchronization, causing data races and potentially a concurrent-map panic when files contain records.
Every input line is copied into the unused raw buffer, so processing a sufficiently large log can consume memory proportional to the entire file and exhaust the process.
A malformed timestamp is silently replaced with the zero time and the record is still counted when no since filter is supplied, producing an incorrect report.
Adding accepted int64 latencies can overflow total, causing the reported average to be incorrect for sufficiently large values or enough records.
If the since filter or input leaves no valid records, dividing by the record count panics instead of returning an empty report or an error.
A negative top value or a value larger than the number of distinct paths causes this slice operation to panic.
A percentile of 100 or an out-of-range percentile is accepted by parsing but indexes beyond the latency slice and panics.
The percentile index uses len(sorted)*percentile, which selects one rank too high at exact percentile boundaries (for example, p50 of two values selects the larger value).

raw_findings.message: Creating the summary with mode `0666` allows group or world access when the process has a permissive umask, potentially exposing or permitting modification of report data.
The gzip command's error is ignored, so the program reports success even when compression fails and leaves the expected compressed output missing.
The output path is concatenated into a shell command, so a crafted `-out` value containing shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary commands.
A zero or negative `-workers` value starts no consumers, leaving the producer blocked on `jobs` while `readFiles` waits forever for results.
Deferring each file close inside the worker loop keeps every processed file open until that worker exits, so processing many files can exhaust the process file-descriptor limit.
Workers concurrently update the shared `counts` map without synchronization, so concurrent input files can trigger a data race or fatal concurrent-map write.
Every input line is copied into `raw`, which is never used, so a large log can consume memory proportional to its full size in addition to the parsed records.
The timestamp parse error is discarded, so a malformed timestamp is accepted as a record with a zero timestamp and can produce incorrect reports.
Summing untrusted `int64` latency values can overflow, causing the reported average to be incorrect for inputs with sufficiently large latencies.
When filtering or parsing leaves no records, this divides by zero and panics instead of returning an empty report or an error.
Slicing with an unchecked `top` value panics when `-top` is negative or exceeds the number of distinct paths.
A percentile of 100 or an out-of-range percentile produces an invalid index and panics; `parsePercentiles` accepts these values without validation.

raw_findings.message: New summary files are created with mode 0666 before umask, so a permissive umask can expose report contents to other users.
The user-controlled output path is concatenated into a shell command, so an output value containing shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary commands with the program's privileges.
The gzip command's error is discarded, so the program reports success even when compression fails and the promised compressed output is not produced.
A zero or negative worker count starts no consumers, so the job sender blocks and the command hangs when any input path is supplied.
Each opened file is deferred for closing until its worker exits, so a worker processing many paths retains every descriptor and can exhaust the process's file limit.
Workers concurrently update the shared counts map without synchronization, causing a data race and potentially a concurrent-map-write panic.
Timestamp parse errors are ignored, so malformed timestamps are accepted as zero-time records and included in summaries when no since filter is set.
When filtering or input leaves no records, average calculation divides by zero and panics instead of returning a summary or error.
The top value is not checked against the available path count or for negativity, so values outside the valid slice range panic.
Percentiles are not restricted to a valid index range, so a valid-looking value of 100 or any value outside 0–100 causes an out-of-range panic for nonempty input.
